note: Static navigable mockups. All figures are demo data.

flows.name: Onboarding
flows.summary: A visitor lands from X, a creator or a referral link, understands the offer and signs in. There is no application: trading is the evaluation.

screens.title: Landing
screens.answers: What is this and why should I care?

screens.title: Public leaderboard
screens.answers: Who is winning seats right now?

screens.title: Public payouts
screens.answers: Does this actually pay? Who got paid, how much and when?

screens.title: Rules
screens.answers: What exactly do I have to do, and what can I lose?

screens.title: Sign in
screens.answers: How do I get in? Same account as onchain.cc.

why.what: A visitor arrives from X, a creator or a referral link, understands the offer, sees the live leaderboard and the rules, and signs in with the same account they use on onchain.cc.
why.why: It is the first contact and has to convince a professional trader in seconds: Bitso's real money, 80% of the profit, no challenge fees and clear rules.

flows.name: Not qualified yet
flows.summary: Phase one. A signed-in trader meets three minimums (10 closed trades, $1,000 perps volume, $100 balance) and appears on the leaderboard. Past onchain.cc activity counts.

screens.title: Home, nothing met yet
screens.answers: What do I need to do to get on the board?

screens.title: Deposit
screens.answers: How do I fund my own trading account?

screens.title: Home, in progress
screens.answers: How close am I?

screens.title: Home, on the leaderboard
screens.answers: I made it. Where do I stand?

screens.title: Choose an alias
screens.answers: How will others see me on the board?

screens.title: Home, new to onchain
screens.answers: I have never traded on onchain.cc. When can I realistically request a seat?

why.what: The trader has signed in but does not meet the minimums to appear on the leaderboard yet: they see what is missing, deposit into their own account and choose an alias.
why.why: Many arrive with no history. Without a short, concrete path to the leaderboard they leave before trading.

flows.name: Competing
flows.summary: The trader is on the leaderboard during a dated cycle. Score, board rank and seat number, the seat map with its cut line, and the requirements needed to request a seat.

screens.title: Home, competing
screens.answers: Am I inside the seats, and what moves my score?

screens.title: Leaderboard
screens.answers: Where am I against everyone else?

screens.title: Leaderboard, around the cut
screens.answers: Who is fighting for the last seats, and how far am I from them?

screens.title: Trader profile
screens.answers: How is the trader above me doing it?

screens.title: Score breakdown
screens.answers: How is my score built and what would raise it?

screens.title: Trade, own account
screens.answers: Trade with my own money while the cycle runs.

screens.title: Stats
screens.answers: How good is my trading, really?

screens.title: Payouts
screens.answers: Who is getting paid from their funded accounts, and how much?

why.what: The trader trades their own money during the cycle and follows their standing: board rank and seat, the seat map, score, stats and the terminal for their own account.
why.why: This is where they spend most of their time and where the volume that pays for the business is generated. They must always know whether they are inside or outside the seats and what they are missing.

flows.name: Seat claim
flows.summary: The cycle closes and a 24 hour request window opens. Everyone on the leaderboard who meets the requirements can request a seat, and withdraw the request until the window closes. When it ends, seats go out in score order and granted accounts are live at once.

screens.title: Home, request window open
screens.answers: The cycle is over. Can I request a seat, and what would I get?

screens.title: Request a seat
screens.answers: Confirm the request for a seat.

screens.title: Home, seat requested
screens.answers: Where am I in the queue and how many seats are left above me?

screens.title: Live request board
screens.answers: Who has requested so far, and where does the cut sit right now?

screens.title: Home, cannot request
screens.answers: Why can't I request a seat this time?

screens.title: Home, already funded
screens.answers: I already hold an account. What does the cycle mean for me?

screens.title: Seat granted, account live
screens.answers: I got a seat. What exactly do I get, and can I trade now?

screens.title: No seat
screens.answers: Why didn't I get one, and when is the next chance?

screens.title: Request window missed
screens.answers: I forgot to request. What now?

why.what: When the cycle closes there are 24 hours to request a seat; the live request board shows who has requested, and when it ends, who gets an account and who does not.
why.why: It is the decisive moment of every cycle. It has to be transparent so nobody doubts how seats are assigned.

flows.name: Operating the funded account
flows.summary: The trader operates Bitso's USDC from the same terminal, with the trailing liquidation level always in view. Orders are only blocked by hard limits (allowed markets, cross margin).

screens.title: Home, funded account
screens.answers: How is my account doing against its rules?

screens.title: Trade, funded account
screens.answers: Trade within the rules, with the risk of each order shown before I send it.

screens.title: Order on a market not allowed
screens.answers: Why can't I send this order?

screens.title: Switch account
screens.answers: Move between my own account and the funded one.

screens.title: Order placed
screens.answers: My order went in. What did it change in my limits?

screens.title: Liquidation locked at the start
screens.answers: I'm 10% up. Where is my liquidation level now, and why won't it rise further?

why.what: The trader trades Bitso's USDC from the same terminal, with the trailing liquidation level always in view, and can switch to their own account without mixing figures.
why.why: A professional needs to see on every order how much room is left before losing the account. That is what sets this product apart from any other terminal.

flows.name: Risk events
flows.summary: Two events the trader must understand at a glance: the funded account liquidated at its trailing level, and a platform incident that closes positions automatically while the account stays active.

screens.title: Account liquidated
screens.answers: My equity reached the liquidation level. What happened and what do I keep?

screens.title: Platform incident
screens.answers: Orders can't reach Hyperliquid. What happened to my positions and my account?

why.what: The two hard moments: the account liquidated when equity reaches its level, and a platform outage that closes positions while the account stays active.
why.why: These are the moments where trust is won or lost. They must explain what happened, what the trader keeps and what they can do next, without ambiguity.

flows.name: Claims
flows.summary: The trader claims profit whenever they want, with every position closed. A claim always takes all profit above the starting size: 80% to their own account, 20% to Bitso. Then the funded account resets to its starting size and liquidation level.

screens.title: Profit to claim
screens.answers: How much can I claim now, and what does claiming do to my account?

screens.title: Claim profit
screens.answers: Confirm the claim: all profit, 80% to my own account.

screens.title: Profit claimed
screens.answers: Did it reach my own account, and where does my funded account stand now?

screens.title: Close positions to claim
screens.answers: I have open positions. What do I need to do to claim?

screens.title: Nothing to claim
screens.answers: My account is not above its start. What can I do?

why.what: The trader claims whenever they want, with every position closed: 80% of the profit goes to their own account and the funded account returns to its starting size.
why.why: Getting paid is the promise of the product. If it is not clear how much is claimed and what happens to the account afterwards, nobody trusts the rest.

flows.name: After the account
flows.summary: One funded account at a time. A trader who loses theirs keeps competing with their own money and can request a seat again when the next cycle closes.

screens.title: Home after losing the account
screens.answers: My account is gone. How do I get another one?

screens.title: Competing again
screens.answers: I'm back on the board. Does my last account count against me?

screens.title: Request a seat again
screens.answers: Cycle 2 closed. Can I request a seat now?

why.what: After losing the account, the trader goes back to competing with their own money and can request a seat again at the next cycle close, with no penalty.
why.why: Keeping the trader who loses is key to growth: every return to the competition brings more volume and more referrals.

flows.name: Deposit and withdraw
flows.summary: The trader's own account. Deposits arrive from any EVM chain or Solana through a personal deposit address that forwards funds to Hyperliquid. Withdrawals go to any address on a chosen EVM network. Claimed profit from the funded account lands here too.

screens.title: Own account balance
screens.answers: How much do I have, and where did it come from?

screens.title: Deposit
screens.answers: Where do I send funds, from which chain, and how long does it take?

screens.title: Deposit arriving
screens.answers: I sent it. Where is my money now?

screens.title: Deposit arrived
screens.answers: Is it in my trading balance?

screens.title: Withdraw
screens.answers: How do I send money out, to which address and network?

screens.title: Confirm withdrawal
screens.answers: Is everything right before it leaves?

screens.title: Withdrawal sent
screens.answers: Did it leave, and when will it arrive?

screens.title: Deposit not credited
screens.answers: I sent a token that is not USDC. What happened to it?

why.what: The own account: the balance and where it came from, USDC deposits from any EVM chain or Solana to a personal address, withdrawals to any EVM address, and what happens when a token that is not USDC arrives.
why.why: Without their own money there is no competition. Moving funds in and out has to be as simple as on an exchange, and clearly separate from the funded account.
